source:
## Markdown, the document subset: ATX headers, bullet lists, fenced
## code blocks and paragraphs. Line-oriented blocks; the inline-level
## subset lives in the markup example.
grammar Markdown version "1.0.0" edition "v2" {
  nl = %x0A
  ws = %x20
  pq = *ws
  ## printable minus backtick: inline text.
  ## printable minus backtick AND minus newline (the rep's follower).
  tchar = %x01-09 / %x0B-5F / %x61-10FFFF
  heading = 1*6%x23 %x20 1*tchar pq nl as heading
  item = pq "* " 1*tchar pq nl as item
  ## The body's only follower is the closing fence, so it keeps
  ## newlines — anything but a backtick. (No pq after the closing
  ## fence: a nullable there defeats the repetition's backtracking.)
  fence = "```" *( %x01-5F / %x61-10FFFF ) "```" nl as code
  para = 1*tchar pq nl as paragraph
  blank = pq nl
  block = blank / heading / fence / item / para
  doc = *block

  entry main: doc

  test {
    accept "# Title\n\nSome text.\n"
    accept "## Section\n- a\n- b\n"
    accept "```\ncode here\n```\n"
    accept "text only\n"
    reject "```\nunclosed\n"
  }
}
